findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Unretained returned mapping forgets handed spend after two native capture interruptions and owner restore
findings.smallest_reproduction: test_replay.py::test_open_native_two_interrupts_preserve_spend[ledgers]; alternate [experiments]. Dispatch once and settle public ledger. Trace interrupts _items on first mapping; independent profile callback interrupts immediate recovery. No monkeypatch of production code. Restore mapping entry to earlier owner-built BudgetLedger then dispatch the original admitted action.
findings.actual_result: Both checkpoints: KeyboardInterrupt propagates; pending buffer contains raw tuple; seal None. After restore dispatch is accepted, executor call count 2. Expected-refusal assertion fails.
findings.expected_result: Previously handed spend must prevent second dispatch; an interrupt itself must neither accept nor permanently poison an unchanged honest reader.
findings.trust_scope: Documented in-process execution-owner handed mapping and ordinary public owner restore. Trace/profile only choose asynchronous exception checkpoints; no production state introspection mutation or forged admission. Known open family independently reproduced, not a new independent root cause.
findings.proposed_correction: Requires a selected stable owner handoff/lifetime/publication guarantee (or explicit relaxation of all-returned-handings promise). Incremental retention could preserve the already copied ledger map in the experiments variant, but cannot recover the ledgers variant interrupted before any first entry retention. More finite retries shift the hole; later mapping reread lacks overwritten history; permanent poison without corruption violates honest recovery. No generic local correction demonstrated sufficient for both obligations.

All six orders of conflicting left/right/extended-left detached observations: no middle conflicting history disappears, every branch refused (6 pass).

Two retained detached handings, omission of account, interrupted normalization, old checkpoint restoration then current restoration: absent returns None; unread barrier survives; old refused; current recovers (1 pass).
Native capture and immediate recovery interruptions at first and second mapping, followed by restore and real gateway dispatch: 2 expected-refusal failures, duplicate calls.

All 16 existing R16 controls executed including ledger normalization scalars, experiments, registration interruption, repeated detached handings, malformed histories, exact barrier stale reconciliation and conflicting observations: 16 pass.
